status: experimental explicit opt-in ordinary-OCR utility only; parent implementation must be measured anew
input: decoded uint8 RGB HxWx3, same orientation and dimensions as baseline; use existing input size limits; preserve original bytes/evidence

thumbnail.dimensions: max(1, round(width*scale)), max(1, round(height*scale)); Python round ties to even
thumbnail.interpolation: OpenCV INTER_AREA on ENCODED uint8 RGB, before linearization; no resize when scale is 1

background.dilation: cv2.dilate(y, ones((25,25), uint8)); centered anchor, one iteration, OpenCV default morphology border
background.smoothing: cv2.GaussianBlur(dilated, (0,0), 9); sigmaY default=sigmaX, OpenCV default BORDER_REFLECT_101 and automatically derived kernel
background.percentile: numpy.percentile(background, 90), default linear interpolation over flattened pixels at index 0.90*(N-1); reference also computes p10 but global arm never uses it

gate: if p90>=0.55 return original RGB pixels exactly; no candidate OCR or diagnostic/quality score is consulted
application: linearize FULL ORIGINAL RGB, multiply every channel by this one scalar, clip to [0,1]; no resize, warp, spatial gain, per-channel white balance, sharpening, mask, denoising or text-dependent selection
encoding: x<=0.0031308 ? 12.92*x : 1.055*x^(1/2.4)-0.055; multiply by 255, numpy.rint ties-to-even, cast uint8; same shape and coordinates
limits: Inverse sRGB is not sensor RAW recovery or measured camera-response inversion.
Clipped/blurred evidence is not recovered. Scalar correction can still change OCR characters and fields.
Do not use the rejected local-illumination or glare/burst functions in this profile.
No acceptance threshold, field validator or model change; ordinary OCR utility does not authorize a document or person.
No automatic retry/union/best-reading policy was tested. Any such selector is a new candidate and needs a new freeze.
Retain baseline and transformed provenance; expose the operation as explicit experimental user choice, never a certified more-correct reading.

Native/browser resampling, float math, percentile and rounding need pixel/outcome parity checks followed by all unchanged DEV/negative metrics and actual phone latency. Python timing is not browser timing.
